the_window_in_time_is_stated_and_the_tz_.description: journalctl's --since and --until are interpreted in the host's LOCAL time while the order specifies UTC instants, and --utc changes only the output. On a non-UTC host the window would be silently shifted -- and a shifted window that happens to miss the eight ids reads exactly like a correct one that misses them.
the_window_in_time_is_stated_and_the_tz_.expected_landed: the host's own offset printed in the same command and reading +0000
the_window_in_time_is_stated_and_the_tz_.expected_not_landed: any non-zero offset, which would mean the window is not the one the order named and the zeros have a different scope in time than the sentence beside them
the_window_in_time_is_stated_and_the_tz_.observed: The record's third line reads: window 2026-10-07 18:00:00 to 2026-10-09 17:00:00 UTC; host tz +0000, printed by date +%z on the host in the same command. Every journal timestamp in the output independently carries +0000, and OLDEST does too. So the --since/--until window IS the UTC window the order specified. This matters more here than on a live read because the window is historical: a one-hour shift could not be caught by anything else in the output.
